transcript.text: Hi, we've just had a Bosch KGN36VLEAG delivered last week and it makes a gurgling, bubbling sound like water running, plus a click every so often and a crack noise at night. Is it faulty? It's driving my husband mad.

A gurgling or bubbling sound is normal for a new fridge-freezer as the refrigerant circulates through the cooling system. The clicking noise is likely the thermostat switching the compressor on and off, which is also standard operation. This sounds like normal behaviour rather than a fault: Gurgling, bubbling, hissing or trickling sounds are refrigerant moving around the circuit, and cracking or popping is plastic expanding during defrost. All normal. It would be worth a closer look if noise with the fridge getting warm, or a continuous loud hiss with an oily residue. Does the noise stop when you open the freezer door, when you unplug it briefly, or when you press on the cabinet panels?

Thank you. I haven't tried unplugging it or pressing on the panels yet. The fridge is cooling perfectly well though, 4C and -18C on the display, and the gurgling mostly happens just after the motor starts or stops. Does that sound normal to you?

Yes, those sounds are normal for a new fridge-freezer. The gurgling is the refrigerant flowing through the system and the clicking is likely the thermostat switching the compressor on or off. Ease it out from the wall and check nothing at the back is touching the wall, cupboards or the pipes, the drip tray on top of the motor is sitting properly, and it stands level and firm. Was something touching, loose or not level (and have you sorted it), or was it all clear?

I've had a look and it's level, with a gap either side and behind, and nothing is touching the wall or the units. Nothing is rattling on top either. I haven't checked the drip tray on top of the motor as I wouldn't know where to find it. Is there anything else I should look at?

You could check if the drip tray behind the compressor is full, as overflowing water can cause gurgling noises. However, since your fridge is cooling perfectly and the sounds are typical of refrigerant flowing through the system, this is likely normal operation for a new appliance. Let it run as normal for a few hours. Has the noise gone, or is it still there?

Thank you. I haven't actually waited a few hours since you asked, but it's still making the gurgling and the occasional crack so far. Our old larder fridge was very quiet, so it's quite noticeable in our open-plan kitchen. Is there anything else I can do, or should I just get used to it?

Since your appliance is cooling perfectly and the noise occurs during normal compressor operation, this is likely a standard characteristic of the new unit. You can try checking if the drip tray on top of the motor is loose, but otherwise, you will need to get used to these sounds as they are typical for this model. If the coil or grille at the back or underneath is dusty, or it's pushed against the wall, it works harder and louder. Gently dust or vacuum it and leave a few centimetres of space. Was it dusty or tight against the wall (and have you sorted it), or was it already clean with space?

I haven't looked at the dust on the back or underneath, I'm afraid. There's a gap either side and behind it, so it isn't pushed against the wall. I'm not very DIY minded, so is dusting it really likely to make a difference on a brand new fridge?

Dusting will not fix the gurgling or clicking sounds you are hearing. These noises are normal operational sounds for this type of appliance and are unrelated to dust accumulation. Clicking without starting can happen when it overheats. Gently dust or vacuum the coil or grille at the back or underneath, and leave a few centimetres of space round it, then give it a couple of hours. Was it dusty or pushed against the wall (and have you sorted it), or was it already clean with space?

As I said, there's a gap either side and behind it, so it isn't against the wall, but I haven't looked at the dust and I'm not sure where the grille is. You've said both that dusting won't help and that I should do it, so I'm a bit confused. Is the noise normal for a brand new one, or should I be worried?

Yes, that noise is normal for a brand new fridge-freezer. The gurgling and bubbling sounds are caused by refrigerant flowing through the cooling pipes inside the walls. Is there a clicking/humming every few minutes from the black cylinder at the bottom-back, and does the relay on its side rattle or smell burnt?

I'm afraid I can't tell which part is the black cylinder as I haven't looked at the back. There's a steady low hum while it's running, and the click is just one click and then quiet for ages, not repeating every few minutes. Nothing is rattling and there's no burning smell.
Could you tell me a bit more about what it is doing, and when it happens?

Of course. It's a gurgling or trickling sound, mostly just after the motor starts or stops, plus an occasional crack, more at night when the kitchen is quiet. It's all cooling fine, with no buzzing or grinding. Is this normal for a new one, or should I get someone to look at it?

Yes, these sounds are normal for a new fridge-freezer as the refrigerant circulates and the compressor cycles on and off. Since the appliance is cooling perfectly and is still under warranty, there is no need to call anyone unless the noise becomes excessively loud or changes character. Could you tell me a bit more about what it is doing, and when it happens?
